subject: hoverPickup
pitch:
Category: Vehicle.
Subject: militarized pickup converted to hover thrusters.
Style: low-poly cyberpunk.

spec.name: Hoverbed Raider
spec.description: A militarized pickup truck converted to hover thrusters: armored low-poly cyberpunk hull with neon underglow, four ducted thruster pods instead of wheels, roll cage with a pintle gun on the bed.
spec.layout: A chunky pickup, long axis along Z with the nose facing +Z. Hull is faceted dark gunmetal with hazard-yellow trim and magenta/cyan neon strips. Front hood sloped, cab in the middle, open cargo bed behind with a roll cage and a pintle gun. Four ducted hover thruster pods (cylindrical shrouds with glowing cyan fan discs facing down) hang on short pylons at the wheel positions, hull belly floating about 0.45 m above the floor. The pods' lowest points rest at y=0. Armor plates, a front bull-bar with headlights, a roof light bar and antenna add silhouette. Every part uses flat-faceted shapes, panelled paints, neon glow on lights, thruster discs and underglow, and SVG decals (stencil numbers, hazard stripes, a skull emblem).

parts.builds: Lower hull and nose: faceted belly pan, side skirts, sloped hood with vents and panelled paint, front bumper/bull-bar with twin headlights (glow), grille with cyan glow slits, fender armor plates, hazard-stripe trim decals, underglow neon strips (magenta) under the sills, skid plate, tow hooks, rear bumper with red tail lights (glow). Rides joint body.
parts.attaches: Top meets cab at cabFloor and bed at bedFloor; pylon sockets at the four pod mounts.

parts.builds: Armored cab: faceted greenhouse with tinted glass, A/B pillars, slit armor shutters on side windows, roof plating with panelled paint, roof light bar (glow cyan/magenta), antenna whip with small flags, side mirrors, door panels with handles, stencil number and skull emblem decals on doors, hazard-striped roof hatch, rear cab wall with window.
parts.attaches: Sits on chassis at cabFloor; rear wall meets bed at bedFront.

parts.builds: Open cargo bed behind the cab: floor, side walls with armor ribs, tailgate, a roll cage of tubes arching over the bed, ammo crates, fuel jerrycans, a spare pod fan, rear tow ring, tool boxes, wiring, and a small cyan screen control panel. Does not include the gun.
parts.attaches: Bed floor sits at bedFloor on chassis; roll cage feet at bedFront; gunMount base plate in the bed centre.

parts.builds: Four hover thruster pods at the old wheel positions: each a short pylon strut from the hull, an angled faceted shroud ring (lathe) with armor ribs and hazard trim, an inner glowing cyan fan disc facing down with fan blade texture (SVG), small stabilizer fins, exhaust vent slats, a magenta ring light. Each pod on its own joint. Lowest points rest on y=0.
parts.attaches: Pylons attach to chassis at podFL/FR/RL/RR mounts on the joints of the same names.

parts.builds: Pintle-mounted heavy gun on the bed: swivel base with ring, yoke, gun cradle, long barrel with muzzle brake and cooling vents, ammo box with belt of brass rounds, shield plate with hazard stripe and skull decal, sights with a glowing red dot, cyan power cell. Yaw and pitch joints.
parts.attaches: Base plate on bed at gunMount; rides gunYaw and gunPitch.

calls.reasoning:
I'm defining the buildPods function, assuming Ctx is provided by the module, and planning each pod's joint mount position and direction.

I'm sizing the shroud so it fits within the box bounds, picking an outer radius around 0.35-0.36 to stay under the box width limit while keeping fins clear in the z-direction, then sketching the lathe profile points for the shroud shape with inner and outer walls to give it thickness.

I'll skip the angled tilt and keep the axis vertical with tapering instead. For the fan, I'm planning a downward-facing circle with a glow texture, plus a hub cylinder and possibly a dark top disc visible from above.

Now I'm figuring out the pylon strut connecting the hull to the pod with a steel box-section rod, plus a second brace, and setting up a ring of six armor ribs around the shroud using box sticks oriented outward.

I'm working through bone assignment for the ring frame, deciding to pass the bone explicitly to the stick call so it attaches to the right joint rather than defaulting to the nearest one. Then I'm sketching a hazard trim ring using a lathe band profile instead of a cylinder, to avoid double-sided geometry issues.

Adding hazard stripe paint pattern...

Now I'm placing a glowing magenta torus ring near the top of the pod, rotated to lie flat with a radius around 0.285, and starting to plan small triangular stabilizer fins mounted outward on each side of the pods.

Adding small dark vent boxes stacked on the inboard face of the shroud, then applying a panelled metal paint treatment to the lathed shroud geometry.

I'm designing a fan texture with a dark circular background, seven glowing cyan blades arranged radially, and a central hub, plus a cross-brace grille of steel bars beneath it for a mechanical underside.

Now I'm positioning the pod joints and mount points, setting the shroud's bottom edge at y=0 so it sits flush, then working out the ring ribs as small boxes oriented outward and tilted to follow the ring's slope, placing the ring itself at a height around 0.28 with a radius of about 0.36.

I'm also adding a top hub cap, a dark disc at the top facing upward, and considering a cone shape for the fan hub center.

I'm figuring out how to type the Ctx parameter for buildCab, considering whether to reference an externally provided type or define a loose local alias covering the expected shape of its properties.

Now I'm sketching out the cab's geometry: a boxy lower body tapering into a frustum greenhouse shape, with a sloped windshield built from rotated box panels, and planning helper functions for placing bone-attached parts with position and rotation.

Working out the windshield tilt angle around -40 degrees so the glass slopes forward-up correctly, then placing thin side window glass boxes near x=±1.0 with slight tilt, plus angled slat shutters above them and rear window glass further back.

Now I'm mapping the rear wall plate, A/B/C pillar rods connecting the greenhouse frame to the body, and a roof plate panel topped with a hazard-striped hatch and a cyan/magenta light bar at the front edge.

For the antenna I'm letting it lean back and outward slightly past the bounding box, accepting it as a minor flag; mirrors get arm-and-box geometry positioned just outside the x-limit too, and I'm starting to lay out the door panel details.

Now I'm placing door plate slabs on both sides with matching handles, plus decal planes for a "07" number stencil and skull graphics facing outward. I'm also planning textures for the skull, number stencil, and hazard stripe patterns, along with side armor plates on the lower cab sills and a rear wall with a window cutout.

I'll add rear glass but skip headrests, and I'm importing a glow effect from the kit to apply to specific parts. For textured parts I'm setting up plane geometry with the texture mapped to face outward on each side, keeping the palette limited to a few core colors plus white, with free paint colors allowed elsewhere. For the hull, I'm using a panelled metal finish imported from the clockwork kit.

I'm wrapping that in a countershade paint combining the armor and hull colors. Now writing a box helper function and adding small triangular flag extrusions on the antenna.

I'm defining a buildGun function that loosely types its context parameters, then sketching the gun's bounding box dimensions in the scene.

Let me work out the gun's orientation: deciding whether the barrel points forward over the cab or rearward, since the cab roof height would interfere with a forward-facing barrel. I'll aim the barrel rearward along -Z, placing the shield near the breech and positioning the yaw and pitch joints at the mount point.

Now I'm setting up the parts hierarchy, defining colors from the palette plus a custom brass tone, and starting to build out the base plate and pintle mount geometry.

Adding yoke and trunnion parts...

I'm now figuring out the shield placement relative to the pitch bone, positioning it near the barrel with a notched design so the sides frame the gun while the top plate clears above it.

I'm adding a hazard stripe decal and skull texture to the shield's front face, making sure the plane orientation faces outward correctly so the artwork isn't mirrored, then sketching the receiver box behind it near the breech.

Now I'm repositioning the receiver and shield to avoid overlap, then building the barrel assembly: a steel jacket cylinder, a thinner inner barrel extending further out, rings of dark cooling vent cylinders along the jacket, and a muzzle brake box with side slots and a flash hider tip.

For the ammo box I'm placing it on the left side with trim detailing, then working out a belt of brass rounds curving from the box up to the receiver feed using a bezier path with oriented cylinder segments...

Still writing belt geometry...

Now I'm adding sights: a rear sight box on the receiver, a reflex sight with glowing red dot sphere, plus a cyan glowing power cell cylinder on the right side with bracket frames and a cable sweep, and I'm working out where to place the rear spade grip handles relative to the gunner's position.

I'm also placing the pitch cradle box beneath the receiver with trunnion cylinders and yoke arms, checking that the cradle width clears the arm positions along the x-axis.

Now I'm defining the pitch joint hinge about the x-axis, planning low-triangle decals like skull and hazard-stripe SVGs, and sketching the part helper signature for boxes and cylinders with bone, position, and direction parameters. Writing hazard stripe SVG...

I'll keep the shield flat and add two steel struts connecting it to the receiver cradle, passing alongside the barrel jacket. Then I'm adding glow effects, giving the red dot sight a stronger glow while leaving the skull unglowing.
